title: Yash's Toxic Crosses $120,000 in US Advance Ticket Sales Ahead of Release
excerpt: The KGF star's next film has sold over 5,500 tickets across 204 US locations with Texas leading the charge, while overseas and domestic pre-release deals have already crossed ₹225 crore.
body:
• Toxic has grossed $121,258 in US advance ticket sales across 204 locations and 589 shows, with over 5,550 tickets sold and daily additions of roughly $10,000.
  • Texas leads all US states with $47,000 and nearly 2,000 tickets sold, followed by California at $19,244 — reflecting strong South Indian diaspora demand in both markets.
  • The Telugu version accounts for $66,896 of the US total, outpacing the Kannada version at $54,363, signaling the KGF franchise's growing pan-South-Indian appeal.
  • Pre-release business has already crossed ₹225 crore, including a record overseas deal of ₹105 crore from Phars Film and an AP-Telangana deal of ₹120 crore from SVC.
https://youtube.com/watch?v=f5M1d7r2UNQ

Texas and California Drive Early Demand

Yash's Toxic has racked up $121,258 in US advance ticket sales, a strong early signal for the Kannada star's first major release since the KGF franchise turned him into a pan-Indian box office force. The film is tracking across 204 US locations with 589 scheduled shows, and the daily addition rate of approximately $10,000 suggests the final advance total could climb significantly before opening day.

https://x.com/TheCineNation/status/2089261880632049716

Texas has emerged as the strongest market, generating $47,000 from nearly 2,000 tickets — an outsized share driven by the state's large Telugu-speaking population concentrated in the Dallas-Fort Worth and Houston metropolitan areas. California follows at $19,244 with 888 tickets, with the Bay Area and Los Angeles anchoring demand.

Cinemark theaters account for $98,128 of the total — more than 80% — reflecting the chain's dominant position in South Indian film distribution across the US. The concentration in a single exhibitor also highlights the niche nature of Indian-language releases in North America, where screen counts remain a fraction of what Hindi or Hollywood releases command.

Telugu Version Outpaces Kannada in the US

In a notable shift, the Telugu-dubbed version of Toxic has outsold the original Kannada version in US advance sales: $66,896 versus $54,363. The pattern mirrors what happened with KGF Chapter 2, where the Telugu market eventually contributed more to the worldwide gross than the Kannada original.

"The Telugu market's embrace of Yash is no longer a spillover from KGF — it's a standalone fan base that treats his releases as events."

— Sacnilk box office analysis

For Yash, this cross-linguistic appeal is central to his commercial viability as a pan-Indian star. Toxic is releasing in Kannada, Telugu, Tamil, Hindi and Malayalam — a five-language strategy that only a handful of Indian actors can support with genuine audience demand in each market.

Record Pre-Release Deals Signal Industry Confidence

The pre-release business for Toxic has already crossed ₹225 crore across domestic and international territories. Phars Film, a leading overseas distributor of Indian films, secured the international rights for a reported ₹105 crore — a record for a Kannada-origin film. SVC picked up the Andhra Pradesh and Telangana theatrical rights for ₹120 crore, another benchmark figure.

These numbers reflect the premium that distributors are willing to pay for a proven franchise star. The KGF duology grossed over ₹1,250 crore worldwide, and distributors are betting that Toxic — despite being an original property rather than a sequel — can tap into the same audience.

The Film and Its Star Power

Toxic stars Yash alongside Kiara Advani, Nayanthara, Huma Qureshi and Tara Sutaria — a multi-industry cast that underscores the film's pan-Indian ambitions. The screenplay is co-written by Yash himself, with direction by Geetu Mohandas, known for her critically acclaimed Malayalam films Liar's Dice and Moothon.

"Cinema has no owners. A film's success belongs to the audience."

— Yash, at the Toxic trailer launch

The pairing of Mohandas's arthouse sensibility with Yash's mass-market stardom is an unusual creative bet. Whether it produces a film that satisfies both the KGF action audience and critics who have championed Mohandas's earlier work remains the central question heading into release.

What the Numbers Mean for Opening Weekend

US advance sales of $120,000-plus two weeks before release place Toxic in competitive territory for a South Indian film, though still well behind the benchmarks set by Telugu tentpoles from stars like Ram Charan and Jr NTR. The trajectory — adding $10,000 daily — suggests a US opening weekend in the $2-4 million range if momentum holds, which would rank among the stronger Kannada-origin openings in North America.

The domestic pre-release business of ₹225 crore means Toxic needs a worldwide gross north of ₹350-400 crore to be comfortably profitable for its distributors. For Yash, who has staked significant creative capital on a non-sequel original, the opening weekend will answer whether his star power extends beyond the KGF brand.
nri_angle: Strong US advance sales led by Texas and California reflect the growing box office clout of the South Indian diaspora, with Telugu-speaking audiences driving demand.
